what: The arm's properties are held by functional tests, not by reading the source. Each mutant is a one-change edit of the arm's sources (contracts/account-evm-k256.compact, contracts/modules/EvmK256.compact, and the modules the arm's core, identity and format moved into: contracts/modules/K256Core.compact, contracts/modules/EvmIdentity.compact, contracts/modules/Eip712V1.compact), compiled --skip-zk in its own copy and run against the offline layer (every file of npm run test:evm_k256-offline, the shared wallet-arms suites, constraint-negative-offline and the viem cross-check) and the prover suite's JavaScript layer (EVM_K256_DRY=1, no proof server, every section), where a mutant that lets a refused forgery through fails that case's simulator half. A mutant is killed when a suite shows its effect: an accepted forgery (a call the unmutated copy refuses goes through), a broken honest call, or a changed output; a suite that only reports another refusal message does not count as a kill. The unmutated copy, compiled and run the same way, passes every suite (the control).

mutants.mutation: the zero-scalar assert deleted (r != 0 and s != 0: one assert in K256Core, which every seam's verification calls)
mutants.killKind: changed output at K256Core alone (r = 0 no longer refused; the verification returns false); no forgery a test can build
evidence: k256-core-probe-offline (probe-k256-core): ✗ r = 0 is refused at the core (the honest key, digest and s) (NOT refused: the core accepted it); the pure circuit returned false
offline: evm-k256-seam-offline (r, s) = (0, 0) refused by "secp256k1 scalar field has no inverse for 0"; evm-k256-grants-offline r = 0 refused by "invalid grant signature"
prover: 16/16 r = 0 forgeries refused at /check (constraint), 17/17 s = 0 forgeries refused by the witness computation (cannot invert zero); 33/33 controls proved
mutants.review: reviewed (cross-agent audit, round 1): not equivalent; reclassified
mutants.argument: Not equivalent: with r = 0, u2 = r/s = 0, so a signature verifies exactly when x(u1·G) is 0 mod n. That point exists (x = n is below the field prime, and (n, 0x98f66641cb0ae1776b463ebdee3d77fe2658f021db48e2c8ac7ab4c92f83621e) is on the curve), so for its discrete logarithm k, any non-zero digest scalar z and s = z/k give a signature with r = 0 that verifies under every key. No test can build that input (it needs k), and every r = 0 forgery a test can build is refused without the assert (the proof-server runs below). At K256Core alone the deletion is observable: r = 0 is no longer refused and the verification returns false, which k256-core-probe-offline catches. The assert stays: it refuses r = 0 outright instead of resting on the hardness of a discrete logarithm.

mutants.mutation: O1 r != 0 deleted (s != 0 kept)
mutants.killKind: changed output at K256Core alone (r = 0 no longer refused; the verification returns false); no forgery a test can build
evidence: k256-core-probe-offline (probe-k256-core): ✗ r = 0 is refused at the core (the honest key, digest and s) (NOT refused: the core accepted it); the pure circuit returned false
offline: r = 0 refused by "invalid (grant) signature" instead of the zero-scalar message
prover: P16's runs, the 16 r = 0 forgeries
mutants.review: reviewed (cross-agent audit, round 1): not equivalent; reclassified
mutants.argument: Not equivalent: with r = 0, u2 = r/s = 0, so a signature verifies exactly when x(u1·G) is 0 mod n. That point exists (x = n is below the field prime, and (n, 0x98f66641cb0ae1776b463ebdee3d77fe2658f021db48e2c8ac7ab4c92f83621e) is on the curve), so for its discrete logarithm k, any non-zero digest scalar z and s = z/k give a signature with r = 0 that verifies under every key. No test can build that input (it needs k), and every r = 0 forgery a test can build is refused without the assert (the proof-server runs below). At K256Core alone the deletion is observable: r = 0 is no longer refused and the verification returns false, which k256-core-probe-offline catches. The assert stays: it refuses r = 0 outright instead of resting on the hardness of a discrete logarithm.

mutants.mutation: O1 s != 0 deleted (r != 0 kept)
mutants.killKind: message only (offline); refused at the proof server
mutants.equivalence: s ≠ 0 deleted, r ≠ 0 kept: an input with s = 0 and r ≠ 0 meets the same circuit as P16's, and P16's proof-server runs refuse every s = 0 forgery (the in-circuit inverse of 0 has no witness); (0, 0) is still refused by the r ≠ 0 assert. The offline suites refuse s = 0 with another message ("secp256k1 scalar field has no inverse for 0").
evidence: offline: s = 0 refused by the runtime's inverse of 0
prover: P16's runs, the 17 s = 0 forgeries

mutants.review: reviewed (cross-agent audit, round 1): equivalent through the arm only; killed at the core
mutants.throughTheArm: equivalent: No input distinguishes it: with K256Core's key rule deleted, the point at infinity still has no address. Extracting the coordinates of its flagged encoding fails in the circuit (and in the runtime), and its unflagged encoding (0, 0) is not a point of the curve (the circuit's point assignment, and the honest decoder, refuse it). The offline suites pass (every infinity key is refused by the runtime's checks); the prover suite's JavaScript layer cannot build its patched copies (the key rule's text is gone, a harness limitation, not a kill). At the proof server, against the mutant's own full key generation with the bypass lists naming only the asserts it still has (sections activation, seam and core): all 19 key-at-infinity forgeries (the activation, flagged and unflagged; every one of the 15 gated exports with an entry or grant planted for the identity's address and a signature that verifies against it; the device seam) refused, 18 by a constraint of the circuit under test at /check, the unflagged activation key by the proof server's input decoding, each after the honest call proved through the same patched copy. The key rule is the extra safety check its comment names.
